source_of_record: Weller M et al. EANO guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of diffuse gliomas of adulthood. Nat Rev Clin Oncol 2021;18:170-186 (CC BY 4.0); Stupp R et al. N Engl J Med 2005;352:987-996.
_note: Evidence quotes are filled verbatim from the source PDF by extract_eano_quotes.py and gated by verify_eano_quotes.py (verbatim=true only if the quote is a substring of the PDF text). Value fields are corrected per the guideline body. source_version stays 'EANO 2021'; post-2021 updates live in post_guideline_updates.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: Karnofsky performance score (KPS), neurological function, age
global_recommendations.quote: Karnofsky performance score (KPS), neurological function, age, and individual risks and benefits should be considered for clinical decision-making.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: Treatment decisions in patients with glioma are made based on tissue diagnosis
global_recommendations.quote: Treatment decisions in patients with glioma are made based on tissue diagnosis, including the assessment of molecular markers relevant for diagnosis; therefore, upfront surgery is commonly performed with both diagnostic and therapeutic intent.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: When microsurgical resection is not safely feasible
global_recommendations.quote: When microsurgical resection is not safely feasible (for example, owing to the tumour location or the impaired clinical condition of the patient), a stereotactic biopsy should be performed.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: Clinical decision-making without obtaining a tissue diagnosis
global_recommendations.quote: Clinical decision-making without obtaining a tissue diagnosis should be considered only in very exceptional situations.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: The extent of resection is a prognostic factor
global_recommendations.quote: The extent of resection is a prognostic factor and thus, efforts at obtaining complete resections are justified across all glioma entities.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: In the current surgical approach to gliomas, the prevention of new permanent neurological deficits
global_recommendations.quote: In the current surgical approach to gliomas, the prevention of new permanent neurological deficits has higher priority than the extent of resection.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: The use of evoked potentials, electromyography or brain mapping in awake patients
global_recommendations.quote: The use of evoked potentials, electromyography or brain mapping in awake patients under local anaesthesia to monitor and preserve language and cognition facilitates resections in eloquent areas41.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: Radiotherapy should start within 3-5 weeks after surgery
global_recommendations.quote: Radiotherapy should start within 3-5 weeks after surgery48 and is commonly administered at 50-60 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy daily fractions.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: Hypofractionated radiotherapy with a higher dose per fraction
global_recommendations.quote: Hypofractionated radiotherapy with a higher dose per fraction and a lower total dose (for example, 15 × 2.67 Gy) is appropriate in older patients (>65-70 years of age) and in those with a poor prognosis (typically defined by a KPS of <70)54.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: Watch-and-wait strategies without histological verification carry the risk
global_recommendations.quote: Watch-and-wait strategies without histological verification carry the risk of underestimating the grade of malignancy when determined using only neuroimaging and thus require initial intervals of only 2-3 months between scans.

global_recommendations.start_phrase: After the completion of therapy, an initial interval between scans of 2-6 months
global_recommendations.quote: After the completion of therapy, an initial interval between scans of 2-6 months is common practice for most patients depending on the disease histology but longer intervals might be appropriate in NaTure RevIeWS | ClInIcAl Oncology evidence-Based guidelines volume 18 | March 2021 | 177 cases of durable disease control and more benign tumours.

items: continuing any treatment beyond confirmed progression on that treatment (including bevacizumab and TTFields)

applies_to: IDH-mutant grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma with residual/measurable disease after surgery, not candidates for immediate RT or chemotherapy
recurrent grade 2 non-enhancing disease in RT/chemo-naive patients
post_guideline_updates.statement: Vorasidenib (a dual mutant IDH1/IDH2 inhibitor) is an option; in the INDIGO phase 3 trial median PFS was 27.7 vs 11.1 months. Adult dose 40 mg once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
post_guideline_updates.copilot_wording: Not part of EANO 2021; per the INDIGO trial and current approvals, an IDH inhibitor (vorasidenib) is an option for residual/recurrent IDH-mutant grade 2 glioma when RT/chemotherapy is deferred.

glioblastoma:4.first_line_adjuvant: Temozolomide chemoradiotherapy: radiotherapy 60 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy fractions (Table 2: 54-60 Gy) with concomitant temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily during radiotherapy, then maintenance temozolomide 150-200 mg/m2 on days 1-5 of 28-day cycles (Stupp regimen; age <70).
glioblastoma:4.age_branch: Operational cutoff 70 years (guideline text writes 65-70). Age <70 with KPS >=70: temozolomide chemoradiotherapy. Age <70 with KPS <70: hypofractionated radiotherapy (40 Gy in 15 fractions, ~2.67 Gy). Age >=70: MGMT-methylated -> temozolomide chemoradiotherapy or temozolomide alone; MGMT non-methylated/unknown -> hypofractionated radiotherapy. KPS <50 or unable to consent: best supportive / palliative care.
glioblastoma:4.at_progression: Nitrosourea; temozolomide rechallenge; re-resection; re-irradiation; bevacizumab for symptom control; standards at recurrence are less well defined.

evidence.start_phrase: Surgery for glioblastoma should involve gross total resection
evidence.quote: Surgery for glioblastoma should involve gross total resection whenever feasible46.

evidence.start_phrase: Concomitant radiotherapy and chemotherapy with temozolomide (75 mg/m2 daily
evidence.quote: Concomitant radiotherapy and chemotherapy with temozolomide (75 mg/m2 daily throughout radiotherapy, including at weekends) plus six cycles of maintenance temozolomide (150-200 mg/m2, 5 out of 28 days) is the standard of care for adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma who are in good general and neurological condition and are aged <70 years59.

evidence.start_phrase: Patients with unfavourable prognostic factors (defined by age and/or KPS) can be treated with hypofractionated radiotherapy (such as 40 Gy in 15 fractions)
evidence.quote: Patients with unfavourable prognostic factors (defined by age and/or KPS) can be treated with hypofractionated radiotherapy (such as 40 Gy in 15 fractions), which has similar activity to irradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions54.

evidence.start_phrase: The addition of temozolomide to hypofractionated radiotherapy
evidence.quote: The addition of temozolomide to hypofractionated radiotherapy54 has also been shown to improve OS in patients aged ≥60 years94.

evidence.start_phrase: patients with tumours lacking MGMT promoter methylation or of unknown
evidence.quote: patients with tumours lacking MGMT promoter methylation or of unknown MGMT promoter methylation status should be treated with hypofractionated radiotherapy alone whereas those with tumours with MGMT promoter methylation status should receive temozolomide alone (5 out of 28 days until disease progression or for 12 months)97.

evidence.start_phrase: The standard of care for patients with IDH-wild-type glioblastoma aged <70 years
evidence.quote: The standard of care for patients with IDH-wild-type glioblastoma aged <70 years and with a KPS >70 includes resection as feasible or biopsy followed by involved-field radiotherapy and concomitant radio therapy and six cycles of maintenance temozolomide chemotherapy (EORTC 26981-NCIC CE.3)59.

evidence.start_phrase: Temozolomide might only be active in patients with MGMT
evidence.quote: Temozolomide might only be active in patients with MGMT promoter-methylated tumours whereas its activity in patients with MGMT promoter- unmethylated tumours is probably marginal95.

evidence.start_phrase: Elderly patients not considered candidates
evidence.quote: Elderly patients not considered candidates for temozolomide chemoradiotherapy should be treated on the basis of MGMT promoter methylation status (NOA-08, Nordic Trial) with radiotherapy (such as 15 × 2.66 Gy) or temozolomide (5 out of 28 days) alone96,98,97.

evidence.start_phrase: At recurrence, standards of care are less well defined
evidence.quote: At recurrence, standards of care are less well defined.

corrections_applied.hypofractionation: 40 Gy in 15 fractions (2.67 Gy; recommendation text: 15 x 2.66 Gy)

astrocytoma:4.first_line_adjuvant: Temozolomide chemoradiotherapy (54-60 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy fractions), potentially without concomitant temozolomide (radiotherapy followed by temozolomide). Evidence is extrapolated from IDH-mutant anaplastic (grade 3) astrocytoma and glioblastoma trials rather than dedicated trials - state this explicitly.
astrocytoma:4.age_branch: No specific age rule; KPS-based intensity caveat applies.
astrocytoma:4.at_progression: Nitrosourea; temozolomide rechallenge; bevacizumab for symptom control.

evidence.start_phrase: Tumours formerly diagnosed as IDH-mutant glioblastoma are now referred to as
evidence.quote: Tumours formerly diagnosed as IDH-mutant glioblastoma are now referred to as IDH-mutant astrocytoma, WHO grade 4, and are managed either as IDH-wild-type glioblastoma or as IDH-mutant astrocytoma, WHO grade 3 (Table 2).

astrocytoma:3.first_line_adjuvant: Radiotherapy 60 Gy (Table 2: 54-60 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy fractions) followed by maintenance temozolomide for 12 cycles (CATNON). The role of concomitant temozolomide during radiotherapy is uncertain - do not present concomitant temozolomide as standard.
astrocytoma:3.observation_eligibility: Wait-and-see is an option per Table 2 in selected cases; radiotherapy is part of first-line for grade >=3.
astrocytoma:3.at_progression: Nitrosourea; temozolomide rechallenge; re-resection; re-irradiation after a minimum interval of ~12 months if the lesion is small.

evidence.start_phrase: The standard of care for patients with this disease subtype is maximal surgical resection or biopsy followed by radiotherapy at 60 Gy
evidence.quote: The standard of care for patients with this disease subtype is maximal surgical resection or biopsy followed by radiotherapy at 60 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy fractions (Table 1).

evidence.start_phrase: The EORTC 26053 trial (CATNON)
evidence.quote: The EORTC 26053 trial (CATNON) of radiotherapy alone, with concomitant or maintenance temozolomide or with both concomitant and maintenance temozolomide showed a significant prolongation of OS in patients receiving radiotherapy followed by 12 cycles of maintenance temozolomide and, thus, this approach should be considered standard of care; however, the role of concomitant temozolomide remains uncertain88.

evidence.start_phrase: For those with disease relapse after radiotherapy, re-irradiation after a minimum interval of
evidence.quote: For those with disease relapse after radiotherapy, re-irradiation after a minimum interval of ~12 months following the first course of radiotherapy is an option, although tumour size and patterns of recurrence limit the option of re-irradiation and the overall efficacy of this strategy remains uncertain in the absence of data from RCTs.

evidence.start_phrase: The standard of care for IDH-mutant astrocytomas, WHO grade 3 includes
evidence.quote: The standard of care for IDH-mutant astrocytomas, WHO grade 3 includes resection as feasible or biopsy followed by involved field radiotherapy and maintenance temozolomide (CATNON)88.

corrections_applied.rt_dose: 60 Gy (text) / 54-60 Gy (Table 2); maintenance TMZ 12 cycles; concomitant TMZ NOT standard

astrocytoma:2.first_line_adjuvant: If treatment is indicated: involved-field radiotherapy 50-54 Gy (50 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions in text) followed by PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine).
astrocytoma:2.observation_eligibility: Wait-and-see for low-risk patients (pragmatic cut-off ~40-45 years, asymptomatic or seizures only, after resection).
astrocytoma:2.age_branch: Radiotherapy is indicated for incomplete resection and/or age >40 years; younger low-risk patients may be observed. RTOG 9802 high-risk = age 18-39 with subtotal resection/biopsy, or age >=40.
astrocytoma:2.at_progression: Temozolomide (or nitrosourea); re-resection; re-irradiation in selected cases.

evidence.start_phrase: Maximal surgical resection, if safely feasible, is the best initial therapeutic approach
evidence.quote: Maximal surgical resection, if safely feasible, is the best initial therapeutic approach84.

evidence.start_phrase: Younger patients (pragmatic cut-off
evidence.quote: Younger patients (pragmatic cut-off ~40-45 years of age) who are asymptomatic or with seizures only, can be managed through observation alone after gross total resection.

evidence.start_phrase: Involved-field radiotherapy (50 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions) should be considered for patients with incomplete resection
evidence.quote: Involved-field radiotherapy (50 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions) should be considered for patients with incomplete resection and/or for patients aged >40 years.

evidence.start_phrase: The RTOG 9802 trial reported a major prolongation of OS
evidence.quote: The RTOG 9802 trial reported a major prolongation of OS with the addition of PCV polychemotherapy to radiotherapy (54 Gy), from 7.8 years to 13.3 years in patients with high-risk WHO grade 2 gliomas who were 18-39 years of age and had undergone a subtotal resection or biopsy or in those aged ≥40 years75.

evidence.start_phrase: The standard of care for IDH-mutant astrocytomas, WHO grade 2 requiring further treatment
evidence.quote: The standard of care for IDH-mutant astrocytomas, WHO grade 2 requiring further treatment includes resection as feasible or biopsy followed by involved field radiotherapy and maintenance PCV polychemotherapy (RTOG 9802)75.

corrections_applied.rt_dose: 50-54 Gy (50 Gy in 1.8 Gy in text)

oligodendroglioma:3.diagnosis_label: Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, CNS WHO grade 3
oligodendroglioma:3.first_line_adjuvant: Radiotherapy 54-60 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy fractions followed by PCV (two large RCTs showed PCV approximately doubled OS). Wait-and-see per Table 2 only in very selected cases.
oligodendroglioma:3.observation_eligibility: Watch-and-wait after complete resection may be considered for younger patients (<40 years) only without CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, after gross total resection, and with no neurologic deficits.
oligodendroglioma:3.age_branch: Age <40 is one of the watch-and-wait conditions but not sufficient alone.
oligodendroglioma:3.at_progression: Second surgery should always be considered; temozolomide; bevacizumab for symptom control.

evidence.start_phrase: In this subtype, the extent of resection is a prognostic factor
evidence.quote: In this subtype, the extent of resection is a prognostic factor78.

evidence.start_phrase: watch-and-wait strategies after complete resection can also be considered for younger patients
evidence.quote: watch-and-wait strategies after complete resection can also be considered for younger patients (<40 years of age) with WHO grade 3 tumours, specifically for those without homozygous CDKN2A/B deletion, although only after gross total resection and in the absence of neurological deficits.

evidence.start_phrase: Two large RCTs showed that the addition of PCV
evidence.quote: Two large RCTs showed that the addition of PCV, either prior to or after radiotherapy, in the first-line of treatment approximately doubled the OS79,80.

evidence.start_phrase: Second surgery should always be considered
evidence.quote: Second surgery should always be considered.

evidence.start_phrase: bevacizumab can be used for symptom control
evidence.quote: bevacizumab can be used for symptom control; however, the antitumour efficacy of bevacizumab is unknown and no evidence supports its combination with cytotoxic agents in this setting.

evidence.start_phrase: Patients with IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendrogliomas, WHO grade 3 should be treated
evidence.quote: Patients with IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendrogliomas, WHO grade 3 should be treated with radiotherapy followed by PCV polychemotherapy (EORTC 26951, RTOG 9402)79,80.

oligodendroglioma:2.diagnosis_label: Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, CNS WHO grade 2
oligodendroglioma:2.first_line_adjuvant: If further treatment beyond surgery is deemed necessary: radiotherapy 50-54 Gy in 1.8-2 Gy fractions followed by PCV.
oligodendroglioma:2.observation_eligibility: Watch-and-wait is justified after gross total resection (and potentially <40 years with incomplete resection if no deficits beyond symptomatic epilepsy).
oligodendroglioma:2.age_branch: Surgery is the primary modality; watch-and-wait after gross total resection, otherwise radiotherapy followed by PCV.
oligodendroglioma:2.at_progression: Temozolomide chemotherapy is standard treatment at progression.
